messages:
maria: Heads up — planning RBAC change for on-prem breakglass role for private deployments. Need input on network controls & KMS integration.
sam: What's the change?
maria: Add role 'breakglass-admin' with jwt->svcacc flow, limited to jumpbox session manager. Only available via bastion ephemeral token. We'll require KMS unwrap via on-prem keystore proxy.
june: We need to ensure DNS doesn't leak internal names to internet (split-horizon). If breakglass sessions resolve controlplane.<customer>.internal -> should be constrained to VPC only. :lock: 
leo: For KMS: would recommend using decrypt proxy running in customer VPC that signs attestation to our control plane, not giving raw key. So we never have plaintext keys. Audit logs must show decrypt request ID.
maria: Agreed. Also need audit log forwarding to customer's Splunk. How do we handle PII redaction? Our plan: forward metadata and hashes, redact payloads.
sam: For network policy, propose eBPF L7 filter to block DNS responses that contain public FQDNs for internal zones, and egress block for kube-system pods except allowed proxies.
june: Agree, but eBPF on customer kernel is heavy. Add fallback: iptables/netpol with DNS proxy that returns NXDOMAIN for external lookup of internal zones.
leo: Vulnerability triage: CVE-2025-9999 in container runtime could allow container to see host netns. Impact for jumpbox? High. Mitigation: require user namespaces + seccomp profile + drop CAP_NET_ADMIN. Also patch runtime ASAP.
maria: Incident flow: if breakglass key used outside expected bastion session, trigger incident channel, revoke role, rotate kms grant, collect audit logs (keystore + dns + bastion) for 24h.
sec-bot: [automated] alert: unusual decrypt call count from svcacc:breakglass-admin at 1699997890 — rate 120/min. Link: https://inc/RED-1234
sam: On that alert, we should block further decrypts at proxy and spin ephemeral denylist for the svcacc. Who will own runbook?
june: I'll own runbook edits. Add steps: 1) isolate bastion, 2) snapshot keystore metrics, 3) rotate grant, 4) reissue minimal scoped creds, 5) notify legal if exfil suspected.
maria: Also add "forensics mode" for 72h where we preserve full packet-capture for relevant on-prem segments. Need customer consent explicit in SLA.
leo: Quick config snippet for netpol:
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-dns-resolve
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: dns-proxy
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
```

maria: Nice. Last Q: audit retention for on-prem customers — default 90d, allow 365d enterprise. Any objections?
leo: No objections. Make retention configurable per tenant and ensure logs are signed (HMAC) before export.
maria: OK I'll update the RBAC PR with these controls and tag @june for runbook. Thanks.
sam: :thumbsup:
